title: Exact Cook–Levin emission chunks
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine, let its state alphabet have a binary code, and let $C,e,c,A,d$ be natural numbers, $x$ a bit string, and $j$ a natural number. The emitter on the packed records for $x$ at cursor $j$ equals the $j$th chunk of the tableau clause-group schedule with horizon $c\,(A(|x|+C(|x|+1)^e+1)^d+1)^2$, when $j$ is at most the schedule's last round; otherwise it is empty. The final round's chunk includes the schedule terminator.
hypotheses_covered: binary code for its state alphabet
replaced: For every source machine, state code, parameters, instance $x$, and cursor $j$, the chunk selector on the body word at $j$ equals the chunk of round $j$ of the pure tableau group list when $j$ is at most the last round, and the empty word otherwise; member counts and the sole-last-terminator convention are preserved.
